contract.requires:
Let Q be a d-state set, A a finite alphabet, q0 an initial state, and f:Q×A→Q a supplied total deterministic transition table. The supplied input law μ on A is rational; zero-mass letters are deleted, r=|supp μ|, and α=min_{μ(a)>0} μ(a). At horizon n≥1, R_n is the set of terminal-state laws generated by arbitrary joint laws on X_1,…,X_n with every one-coordinate marginal X_t~μ. Arbitrary correlations, including dependence on the past state, are allowed. No independence, fixed stochastic kernel, blind-control, or exact accepting-support condition is assumed.

HORIZON-UNIFORM FINITE-POPULATION THEOREM (source-reported)
For integer P≥1, let H=binom(P+d−1,d−1), a_P=d/(2P), and b_P=d/(Pα+d). Vertices are state histograms x∈N^Q of total P. An allocation z∈N^{Q×A} gives an edge x→y when x_s=Σ_a z_{sa}, y_u=Σ_{s,a:f(s,a)=u}z_{sa}, and |Σ_s z_{sa}−Pμ(a)|≤d for each letter. Let G_{P,n} be the terminal histograms divided by P reachable in exactly n graph steps. Then, for every n,

    sup_{p∈R_n} dist_TV(p,G_{P,n}) ≤ d/(2P),
    sup_{g∈G_{P,n}} dist_TV(g,R_n) ≤ d/(Pα+d).

The same constants are independent of n. Also d_H(cl(⋃_{n≥1}R_n), ⋃_{1≤n≤H}R_n)≤a_P+b_P. The argument applies to every finite semigroup, including noncommutative ones, by adjoining a formal initial identity and using f(s,a)=sa; no mixing or semigroup-structure premise is needed.

\section{Finite-population compilation of arbitrarily long constrained processes}\label{sec:population}

The most consequential surviving route changes the representation of an ordered coupling. A population of finitely many deterministic paths replaces the whole joint law; one correlated filler repairs every input marginal simultaneously. Unlike a local approximation of transition probabilities, its error does not accumulate with the horizon. This yields an executable terminal-optimization algorithm for binary-encoded horizons, together with succinct, exactly marginal-correct coupling witnesses. The graph can be very large; the claim concerns its explicitly accounted cost.

\subsection{The exact interface and time-uniform theorem}

Let $Q$ be a set of $d$ states, $A$ a finite alphabet, $q_0\in Q$, and $f:Q\times A\to Q$ a supplied total deterministic transition table. Let $\mu$ be a supplied rational input law. Delete its zero-mass letters, write $r=|\operatorname{supp}\mu|$, and put $\alpha=\min_{\mu(a)>0}\mu(a)$. Let $\mathcal R_n$ be the set of terminal-state laws obtained from \emph{arbitrary} joint laws on $(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ with $X_t\sim\mu$ for every $t$. Correlations and dependence on the past automaton state are allowed. No independence, blind-control, or exact accepting-support restriction is imposed.

For an integer population $P\ge1$, define
\[
H=\binom{P+d-1}{d-1},\qquad a_P=\frac d{2P},\qquad
b_P=\frac d{P\alpha+d}.
\]
The configuration graph has vertices $x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^Q$ with $\sum_sx_s=P$. An allocation $z\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{Q\times A}$ of total $P$ gives an edge $x\to y$ when
\[
x_s=\sum_a z_{sa},\quad y_u=\sum_{s,a:f(s,a)=u}z_{sa},\quad
\left|\sum_s z_{sa}-P\mu(a)\right|\le d\quad(a\in A).
\tag{C1}
\]
Let $\mathcal G_{P,n}$ be the histograms divided by $P$ reachable from $P\delta_{q_0}$ in \emph{exactly} $n$ graph steps, and $\mathcal G_P=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\mathcal G_{P,n}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact marginals, uniformly approximable terminal laws]\label{thm:population}
For every $n\ge1$,
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal R_n}\operatorname{dist}_{\rm TV}(p,\mathcal G_{P,n})\le a_P,
\qquad
\sup_{g\in\mathcal G_{P,n}}\operatorname{dist}_{\rm TV}(g,\mathcal R_n)\le b_P.
\tag{C2}
\]
Consequently, writing $\mathcal R=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\mathcal R_n$,
\[
d_H\left(\overline{\mathcal R},\bigcup_{1\le n\le H}\mathcal R_n\right)
\le a_P+b_P.
\tag{C3}
\]

The elementary integral-flow lemma is standard and proved below. No novelty or priority assertion is made for that lemma or the resulting theorem before literature review.

## Perfect success and scope

The theorem gives an explicit finite horizon that approximates **every** attainable output law of an arbitrary finite deterministic automaton (hence arbitrary finite, noncommutative semigroup), while keeping every input-coordinate marginal exactly prescribed. It computes the closure of the unbounded-horizon attainable set to arbitrary total-variation accuracy, and decides promised fixed-terminal-gap questions. It does not decide exact equality at a cutpoint or exact membership of that closure.

Let Q be a set of d states, A a finite alphabet, q0 an initial state, and f:Q x A -> Q a total deterministic transition function. Let mu be a probability law on A, restrict A to its positive support, and put alpha=min_a mu(a)>0. For n>=1, let R_n be the set of laws of the terminal state f(...f(q0,X1),...,Xn) over all joint laws of (X1,...,Xn) having Xi~mu for every i. Let R=union_{n>=1} R_n, and write TV(p,q)=1/2 sum_s |p(s)-q(s)|.

For a semigroup S and supported alphabet A subset S, take Q=S union {e}, with an adjoined identity e as initial state. Then f(s,a)=sa, f(e,a)=a, and R_n is exactly the product-law polytope. One can omit the new identity if S already has a suitable identity. No commutativity, regularity, mixing, or positivity of transition matrices is assumed.

## 1. Finite configuration graph

Fix an integer D>=1. A configuration is x in Z_{≥0}^Q with sum_s x_s=D. There are

    N(D,d)=binom(D+d-1,d-1)

configurations. Put a directed edge x -> y if there are integers k_{s,a}>=0 satisfying

    y_u=sum_{s,a:f(s,a)=u} k_{s,a},
    |sum_s k_{s,a} - D mu(a)| <= d   for every a.
